threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look for a parking space before remembering the tube runs all night. That shock when you realize there’s no car culture here.
Last night on the 35, a guy started singing '80s pop. Not well, but the whole bus joined in. Felt like an unexpected Brixton karaoke session.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a toddler on a bicycle, weaving through the market stalls, while an old man haggled over the price of a pickled herring.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can hear spontaneous techno parties erupting in the most unexpected places, like a random courtyard or abandoned building, especially on weekends.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local if they’ve perfected the art of dodging the pigeons at Dolores Park. Tourists just stand there, frozen.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy serenade the Muni while a pigeon danced along to the beat. Only in the Tenderloin does a weekday commute turn into a mini concert.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm is in the tiny, unmarked tapas bars where locals gather after work.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they take pictures of the same street art for the tenth time—still marveling at the details while locals have moved on.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You say 'the Loo' for the toilet instead of 'loo,' and suddenly everyone’s side-eyeing you like a tourist.
Caught the 59 last night—two blokes arguing about which chicken shop was better. It was like a live review show on wheels. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Hearing a spontaneous concert in the courtyard while kids play hopscotch on the sidewalk. That's when Neukölln felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you have a spontaneous dance-off in the middle of a street market while nearby cafés keep serving coffee. It's pure Berlin magic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they maneuver through a BART delay. Tourists just stare at their phones; locals weave through the chaos like pros.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo hop off the 21 with a bouquet, casually dodging a pigeon fight. Only in SF do formal and chaotic collide like that.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the locals flock to Park Güell, but half the time, we’re at the plaça just chatting over a drink, keeping it low-key.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll notice them awkwardly holding the metro map upside down, trying to navigate the labyrinthine L2 line on a Monday morning.
